objectives.text: Deter a Russian attack and be able to repel one: the Government Defence Report (19 Dec 2024) treats Russia as a long-term threat to Europe and Finland that will outlast the war in Ukraine, and a June 2026 parliamentary working group repeated it. Money follows: defence spending 2.5% of GDP in 2025, 3.2% planned by 2030 (3% by 2029 was the April 2025 pledge), and an estimated 2.4% of GDP in defence- and security-related spending in 2026 against NATO's 1.5% target.

constraints.text: Geography: the longest EU/NATO land border with Russia, and a southern coast on a gulf where Russian-linked shipping passes freely. Reinforcement is partly offshore - the Forward Land Forces battlegroup (about 600 Swedish soldiers, expandable to 1,200) is based at Boden in Sweden and rotates into Finland, it is not stationed there.

constraints.text: Public finances: the general government deficit was 4.4% of GDP in 2024 and 4.3% in 2025; the Orpo coalition (National Coalition, Finns Party, Christian Democrats, Swedish People's Party; 108 of 200 seats) is cutting EUR 6bn over the term while raising defence spending, which is why the 2030 target is 3.2% and not more.

constraints.text: Dependence on a patron it cannot discipline: the F-35, the DCA, the Arctic cutter contract and the Atlantic guarantee all run through Washington, which in January 2026 threatened an extra 10% tariff on Finland and seven other countries over Greenland and already charges 15% on EU goods. Stubb called the Greenland crisis the hardest for Finland, since it opposes a close ally on sovereignty and territorial integrity.

constraints.text: Law at sea: UNCLOS limits what a coastal state can do in its exclusive economic zone. The Helsinki District Court threw out the Eagle S case on 3 Oct 2025 for lack of jurisdiction (EEZ, not territorial waters); the Court of Appeal revived it in 2026, but the crew has left Finland and the Supreme Court may still intervene. Deterring cable sabotage by prosecution is slow and uncertain.

constraints.text: Coalition politics: the Finns Party and the Christian Democrats block recognition of Palestine that President Stubb says he would sign, and have criticised the 2025 vote declaring settlements illegal; the 2027 election is the next test. Foreign policy is shared between a president who speaks and a government that pays.

paradoxes.text: The shut border protects and isolates in the same stroke. Closing every crossing ended the instrumentalised migration Helsinki calls a Russian hybrid attack, but it also ended contact: on 1 Jul 2026 Russia closed five of its rail crossings with Finland (leaving only Vainikkala) and sent the formal notice on 9 July, while Stubb says Finns must prepare mentally for an eventual thaw. Finland's best card for a future bargain, the border, is the one it has locked.

paradoxes.text: Joining NATO ended Finland's exposure and created a front. Peskov says Finland and Sweden 'reduced relations to zero' by bringing NATO infrastructure to their soil, and Ukrainian drones, diverted by Russian GNSS jamming in the eastern Gulf of Finland, crossed into Finnish airspace in spring 2026, forcing the army to close airspace and sea lanes three times in a month. The alliance that guarantees Finland also ties it to the spillover of someone else's war.

paradoxes.text: The Trump channel buys access and exposes Finland to the man it courts. Stubb's rapport produced the icebreaker memorandum and the Washington hearing, yet in January 2026 Trump put Finland on the list of eight countries facing an extra tariff over Greenland, and Stubb named that crisis the hardest for Finland. The more Finland bets on one American president, the more it must defend Denmark against him.

paradoxes.text: A rules-based order defended with tools the rules do not give. Finland seized the Eagle S (Dec 2024) and the Fitburg (31 Dec 2025) to deter cable sabotage, but the district court ruled it had no jurisdiction in the EEZ and ordered the state to pay the crew's costs; the Fitburg was released after investigation. Each seizure tests the law of the sea that Finland needs to stay intact.

grand_strategy.reading:
Finland runs the strategy of a frontline state that has finally been given the
alliance it avoided for seventy years, and now has to make it real before the
patron's attention drifts. The aim is not to defeat Russia but to be an
unprofitable target: a large reserve army, American aircraft and basing,
Swedish and Nordic depth, a sealed border, and a loud insistence that Ukraine
must not lose. The grade for Russia is therefore rival, not adversary - the
government says it is not an enemy, aims at weakening Russian capacity through
sanctions and deterrence, and keeps the door open to dialogue after a ceasefire
- but the structure under it (Winter War memory, hybrid pressure, the longest
border) is hostile. The Luttwak pattern is that every layer of security adds
a new exposure: NATO membership brought instrumentalised migration, drones and
GNSS jamming; the Trump channel brought the Greenland tariff threat; the
border closure brought a Russian reply and an end to contact; the shadow-fleet
seizures ran into the law of the sea. Two signals that are not rows: Stubb's
habit of speaking both to Trump (golf, icebreakers) and of preparing Finns for
a post-war thaw with Russia, and the quiet extension of the defence memorandum
with Israel in the same years in which the president publicly condemned the
occupation. The open questions for 2027 are the election, whether the 3.2%
path survives the deficit, and whether the Eagle S case ends in a conviction
or in the Supreme Court.

stances.note: Why rival and not adversary: Finland's own line is that Russia is not an enemy but its actions and breaches of international law are opposed (Valtonen, April 2025), and the declared strategy is to support Ukraine, weaken Russia through sanctions and strengthen defence - deterrence and containment, not an aim of Russia's defeat or regime. Yet the Government Defence Report (Dec 2024) calls Russia a long-term threat that will outlast the war, Supo names it the main threat, the eastern border has been shut since December 2023, Russia closed five rail crossings on 1 Jul 2026, and Peskov says Finland and Sweden 'reduced relations to zero'. Stubb (31 Mar 2025) says Finns must prepare mentally for an eventual thaw, so the door is not closed. Bond - grievance: Winter War memory and the 1,340 km border, now sharpened by hybrid pressure (instrumentalised migration, GNSS jamming, cable incidents). Our reading of the grade is C-level on the word itself; the structure is documented by tier 1 sources.

stances.note: The treaty ally and patron: NATO Article 5, the DCA (15 sites, in force 1 Sep 2024, passed by Parliament unanimously), the F-35 (64 aircraft), the Arctic cutter deal signed by Trump and Stubb on 9 Oct 2025. There is visible friction - the January 2026 tariff threat over Greenland, the 15% US tariff on EU goods - which is why the trend is not warming; Stubb calls Greenland the hardest issue for Finland. The presidential channel to Trump is personal (golf, Mar-a-Lago, the White House) and is the reason the grade holds. Bond - affinity: no historical kinship, but a strong sympathy and a security bet that Finland has no alternative to.

stances.note: Member since 1995 (EU Article 42(7) mutual assistance clause). The Orpo government is a pro-security, anti-debt member: it rejects a 2028-34 budget near EUR 2 trillion and any common-debt instrument, insists on conditionality, and joins the net-contributor group, yet pushes the EU hardest on Ukraine finance and the use of immobilised Russian assets. That is friction on the price, not on the structure, so it stays ally and not reluctant ally. The migration policy of the coalition (stricter asylum, time-limited protection) is national. stances.note: Pragmatic and narrowing. Finland follows the EU formula of cooperation, competition and systemic rivalry; it blocked Chinese purchases on security grounds, and the 2025-29 action plan agreed on Stubb's state visit (Oct 2024) is leaner and avoids the Arctic. China is the third source of Finnish imports (9.4%) and fifth export market (4.5%, the lowest since 2009). The Newnew Polar Bear dragged its anchor over the Balticconnector (8 Oct 2023); China called it a storm accident, and the captain is on trial in Hong Kong. Wang Yi met Stubb in Turku on 5 Jul 2026 and Valtonen in Helsinki, with talk of more exchanges. A source using the word partner is the Chinese readout; the grade is our reading of the structure (hence C). Bond - none.

relations_from.summary: Finland closed its whole eastern border from 30 Nov 2023 after asylum seekers without documents were funnelled to the crossings (the government blamed Russia and called it a hybrid attack after NATO accession). Moscow gave no reason; Finland learned from the media and received the formal note on 9 Jul and judged the effect small.

relations_from.summary: On 25 Dec 2024 the tanker Eagle S, linked to Russia's shadow fleet, dragged its anchor about 90 km and damaged Estlink 2 and four telecom cables; Finland seized it. The district court dismissed the case on 3 Oct 2025 (no jurisdiction in the EEZ); the Helsinki Court of Appeal reversed in 2026 and sent it back. Estlink 2 returned to commercial use in June 2025.

relations_from.summary: On 31 Dec 2025 the cargo ship Fitburg (St Vincent and the Grenadines flag, sailing from St Petersburg, 14 crew from Russia, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan) was seized after damaging an Elisa data cable in Estonia's EEZ and an Arelion cable; services were rerouted. The seizure was lifted in January 2026 after Finnish and Estonian investigators finished; one crew member was remanded.
relations_from.note: The ship is not Russian-flagged; the row records the port of departure and the crew, not a state attribution.

relations_from.summary: Strong GNSS jamming in the eastern Gulf of Finland, tied by Western officials to Russia, diverted Ukrainian military drones into Finnish airspace in March-April 2026 (one downed north of Kouvola). In September 2026 police and border guards found the four drones were thrown off course by jamming and wind and were not aimed at Finland; prosecutors closed the cases. The defence forces closed airspace and sea lanes three times in a month in mid-2026.

Investigators have not said whether it was deliberate.

relations_from.summary: NATO Forward Land Forces Finland stood up on 6 Jun 2026 with a Swedish-led battlegroup at Boden and a multinational staff element in Rovaniemi; Allied forces rotate into Finland by exercise and need. At the Ankara summit (7-8 Jul 2026) France, Sweden and Finland announced that French ground forces will join; Denmark, Iceland, Italy, Norway and the UK also intend to contribute.

relations_from.summary: Withdrawal from the Ottawa Convention on anti-personnel mines: instrument deposited 10 Jul 2025, effective 10 Jan 2026, citing the deteriorated security environment after Russia's full-scale invasion; Finland says it will respect other humanitarian law and has begun planning to reintroduce mines. Poland and the Baltic states left the treaty in the same wave.

relations_from.summary: Defence spending path: 2.5% of GDP in 2025; April 2025 pledge of at least 3% by 2029; April 2026 plan for 3.2% by 2030 on the way to the NATO target of 3.5% core spending by 2035; defence- and security-related spending estimated at 2.4% of GDP in 2026 against a 1.5% target. A June 2026 parliamentary working group urged doubling the budget from EUR 7.7bn to above EUR 14bn by 2029.
